summary: Contestants research how administrative support professionals are vulnerable to workplace stress and burnout, then write a professional report and deliver an oral presentation with recommendations. Both a written research paper and a live presentation are required, and entries must follow specific formatting and submission rules. The event is judged on research quality, report writing, and presentation skills.
time_limits: No more than three (3) minutes for setup
No more than seven (7) minutes for the presentation
No more than five (5) minutes for judges’ questions
submission_requirements: Submit one combined PDF file containing Research Paper, Works Cited, BPA Release Form(s), and AI Usage and Documentation Form
Follow the Report format in the Style & Reference Manual (no Title Page required)
Header on first page must include: Contestant ID Number, Edna Renick, Administrative Support Department, and Current Date
Document limited to seven double-spaced, single-sided, numbered pages with one-inch margins (Works Cited not included in limit; graphs, tables, and charts are included)
In-text citations required throughout the paper
Contestant ID is required for all submissions
Materials must follow BPA Graphic Standards and proper use of BPA logo and/or organization’s name
deadlines: National Deadline: April 1, 2027, 11:59 p.m Eastern Time
what_to_bring: One single-sided laptop, notebook, or tablet for presentation (projection equipment and external displays not provided or permitted)
competencies: Apply foundational administrative concepts to analyze workplace changes and emerging issues, assessing their impact on administrative support functions
Conduct comprehensive research using diverse resources and communicate findings through professional reports and presentations, responding to questions with evidence-based reasoning
Prepare a research report following organizational format standards and evaluate findings to offer recommendations

rubric.criterion: Contestant followed Copyright and/or Fair Use Guidelines and Artificial Intelligence Usage & Citation Policy.

Contestant submitted one (1) combined PDF file containing their Research Paper and Works Cited in the correct format according to the Style & Reference Manual, BPA Release Form(s), and AI Usage and Documentation Form.

rubric.description: The introduction and summary are compelling, with strong evidence and a concise, impactful summary.
The argument is well-organized, with smooth transitions and thoroughly expanded points, demonstrating clear reasoning.
Exhibits deep understanding, explaining complex ideas clearly with insightful examples and thorough coverage.
The response is highly original and inventive, with well-integrated resources adding depth and creativity.
Contains very few or no grammar or spelling errors.

rubric.criterion: Contestant followed Copyright and/or Fair Use Guidelines and Artificial Intelligence Usage & Citation Policy

rubric.description: Contestant maintains good eye contact, uses appropriate gestures and body language, and varies their tone and pace adequately.
The presentation content flows adequately, and the contestant demonstrates a clear and well-integrated structure throughout.
Presentation demonstrates a good understanding of the topic and includes relevant and accurate information.
Responses are detailed, insightful, and effectively address the judges' questions.
Setup lasted no longer than three (3) minutes, and the presentation lasted no more than seven (7) minutes.

judging_notes: AI Policy Level 2 Permitted with Citation
Carry-in and setup of equipment must be done solely by the contestant in the allotted time
No Internet access will be provided on-site at NLC; however, contestants may provide their own access to be used only for their presentation to the judges
Judges’ comments will be returned digitally through the online judging system at the national level
Materials submitted for technical judging will not be returned and will not be available at NLC
Props and/or additional items shall not be used as a basis for scoring
PRESENTATION WILL BE STOPPED AT SEVEN (7) MINUTES
eligibility_notes: Any secondary division contestant may enter this judged event.
Contestants must be registered for the national competition before the submission deadline and compete in both parts of the event to be ranked.
Entries that do not follow the provided topic or the Copyright and/or Fair Use Guidelines and Artificial Intelligence Usage & Citation Policy will be disqualified.
Each state is allowed three (3) entries.
